inputs.proposal: Inline the failure backoff step in the J2534 worker: drop j2534_backoff.h and double backoff_ms in place in all three worker modes, capped at J2534_BACKOFF_CAP_MS.
inputs.original_proposal: Inline the failure backoff step in the J2534 worker: drop j2534_backoff.h and double backoff_ms in place in all three worker modes, capped at J2534_BACKOFF_CAP_MS.

questions: Is the change in backoff logic semantically equivalent to the previous implementation? The new logic uses a direct comparison '< J2534_BACKOFF_CAP_MS' instead of checking if the next value would exceed the cap, which could lead to different behavior if backoff_ms is exactly half the cap.

What is the intended behavior when backoff_ms equals J2534_BACKOFF_CAP_MS / 2 (i.e., 2500 ms) in the new logic? The previous implementation would double it to 5000 ms, but the new one caps it at 5000 ms. Is this intended?
nits: Consider adding a comment explaining why the backoff is capped at J2534_BACKOFF_CAP_MS instead of J2 * J2534_BACKOFF_BASE_MS (which would be 200 ms) to avoid confusion about the cap value.
The inline implementation could benefit from a static_assert to ensure that J2534_BACKOFF_BASE_MS is not zero, to prevent potential division by zero or undefined behavior.
